https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c5y3.text: Figure caption, Charred homes, burned out cars - before and after images show Spokane wildfire destruction By Lauren Turner BBC News Published 4 hours ago A man has been arrested on suspicion of arson over the largest of the wildfires that have forced more than 60,000 people to evacuate from the city of Spokane in Washington state. Three major fires have been burning around the north-western state's second-most-populous city since the weekend, with firefighters still working to contain the flames. Aaron Farinacci, 37, was allegedly seen kneeling near grass at the site of the fire and later found to have matches and a lighter, the Spokane County Sheriff said. More than 700 buildings in the area have been destroyed, with another 400 yet to be assessed, and thousands of acres of land have been burned. Washington Governor Bob Ferguson said it was a "nightmare situation", adding: "This is likely the worst natural disaster in Spokane history." The city's mayor Lisa Brown said there was still "the potential for lives to be lost" and that it was too early to say when people might be able to return home. No deaths or injuries have been confirmed. Authorities are trying to make contact with 14 people they have been unable to reach by mobile phone but are not yet considered missing. Sheriff John Nowels said it was likely many of them did get evacuated but had lost signal or had depleted phone batteries. The three fires in the city - Old Trails, Fairview and Autumn Lane - are among a total of 16 wildfires in Washington state, according to the state's department of natural resources. Firefighters have made progress against two of them but while lighter winds and cooler temperatures have been forecast on Tuesday, temperatures are feared to be rising again later this week. Farinacci, who was arrested over the Old Trails fire, is being held on a charge of arson in the first degree and held on a $1m (Â£744,150) bond. Nowels said the Spokane resident had a previous manslaughter conviction. Image source, Reuters Buildings, including homes and businesses, have been destroyed, with videos from the city showing flames tearing through houses as helicopters fly above, trying to put out the flames. Resident Anna Andreachi, who has lost her home, told BBC News partner CBS News: "All of our memories are gone. "My dad just died, and all of his stuff was still in there too." One man who saved his home by digging a fire line said he felt "survivor's guilt" after his neighbour lost theirs. "We're going to open our home to our neighbours," Joe Cvancara said. "I know it's going to take a long time to rebuild." Image source, Reuters Image caption, Tim Hansen, a Spokane resident, carrying a stone angel from the ruins of a burned-out home Governor Ferguson has issued a statewide ban on all outdoor fires. Commissioner of Public Lands Dave Upthegrove said: "Our firefighters are already stretched thin across the state, and with more heat and wind expected this weekend and for the rest of the summer, any new spark on our tinder dry landscapes can lead to another devastating wildfire. "I'm urging all Washingtonians to not be that spark." More than 900 firefighters have been assigned to the Washington fires, with reinforcements expected from other states soon. Scientists have said that human-induced climate change makes the warm, dry conditions that lead to wildfires more likely - as well as leading to more frequent and intense heatwaves and potential summer droughts. https://nineoclock.ro/romanian-budget-ex.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Budget Execution at Eight Months: Deficit Down by Nearly RON 27 Billion Compared with 2025, Falling to 2.89% of GDP Alexandru Nazare, Minister of Finance: It is imperative that we maintain a prudent approach in the period ahead The execution of the consolidated general government budget in the first eight months of 2026 ended with a deficit of RON 59.42 billion , RON 26.94 billion lower than the deficit of RON 86.36 billion recorded during the same period in 2025. In nominal terms, the budget deficit decreased by approximately 31% . As a share of GDP, the deficit fell from 4.51% in the first eight months of 2025 to 2.89% in the same period of 2026 , representing an improvement of approximately 1.62 percentage points . This development reflects the continuation of the fiscal and budgetary consolidation process, with consolidated general government revenues increasing by 11.4% , significantly faster than total expenditure, which rose by 4.2% . Total revenues increased by nearly RON 48 billion compared with the first eight months of 2025, while expenditure increased by approximately RON 21.06 billion . “The eight-month budget execution confirms the continuation of the fiscal consolidation process and the fact that the measures adopted are producing results. It is important that this adjustment is taking place in a context in which revenues are increasing at a significantly faster pace than expenditure, while financing from European funds and the NRRP continues to support the economy and Romania’s development projects. However, it is imperative that we maintain a prudent approach in the period ahead. Every decision concerning public spending must be carefully weighed and made responsibly, given the significant pressures on the budget and the limited fiscal space, as well as external factors that may influence the evolution of Romania’s economy. Therefore, spending discipline, strict prioritisation and maintaining essential investments are mandatory conditions for continuing fiscal consolidation,” said Alexandru Nazare, Minister of Finance. I. CONSOLIDATED GENERAL GOVERNMENT REVENUES Total consolidated general government revenues amounted to RON 468.10 billion in the first eight months of 2026, up 11.4% , or nearly RON 48 billion , compared with the same period in 2025. As a share of GDP, total revenues increased from 21.9% to 22.8% , by approximately 0.85 percentage points . Tax revenues reached RON 242.69 billion , up 14.3% compared with the first eight months of the previous year. A significant contribution came from VAT receipts , which totalled RON 103.35 billion , approximately RON 20.80 billion , or 25.2% , above the level recorded in January–August 2025. Receipts from personal income and wage tax amounted to RON 42.86 billion , up 8.1% , while corporate income tax revenues reached RON 29.55 billion , marking an increase of 9.1% . Social security contributions totalled RON 147.53 billion , approximately RON 9.80 billion , or 7.1% , higher than during the same period in 2025. At the same time, property taxes and levies increased by more than 30% , reaching approximately RON 11.02 billion . Amounts received from the European Union and other donors against payments made and pre-financing amounted to RON 43.38 billion , an increase of approximately 37.7% compared with the first eight months of the previous year. II. CONSOLIDATED GENERAL GOVERNMENT EXPENDITURE Consolidated general government expenditure totalled RON 527.53 billion in the first eight months of 2026, representing a nominal increase of 4.2% compared with the same period of the previous year. At the same time, as a share of GDP, total expenditure decreased from 26.4% in 2025 to 25.7% in 2026 , a reduction of approximately 0.7 percentage points . Personnel expenditure amounted to RON 109.04 billion, down RON 4.26 billion compared with the same period of the previous year, amid reductions in certain allowances for some categories of public-sector employees, as well as measures to limit wage expenditure during 2025–2026. As a share of GDP, personnel expenditure stood at 5.3% of GDP , 0.6 percentage points lower than during the same period of the previous year. Expenditure on goods and services reached RON 67.83 billion , up 7.1% compared with the same period of the previous year. Interest expenditure totalled RON 42.05 billion , an increase of approximately RON 8.86 billion , or 26.7% , compared with the first eight months of 2025. Its share of GDP reached approximately 2% . The evolution of interest expenditure continues to represent a significant pressure on the budget, with fiscal consolidation and reducing financing needs being essential for limiting, over the medium term, the costs associated with public debt. Social assistance expenditure amounted to RON 166.87 billion, down 0.3% compared with the same period of the previous year, taking into account the measures adopted under Law No. 141/2025 on certain fiscal and budgetary measures. Social assistance expenditure was also affected by payments borne by the state budget to compensate electricity and natural gas consumption bills, which amounted to RON 236.64 million during the first seven months of 2026. Regarding the financing of development projects , expenditure related to projects supported by non-reimbursable external funds totalled RON 52.24 billion during the first eight months of the year. The amount includes European funding under the 2014–2020 and 2021–2027 programming periods, European agricultural subsidies, the Modernisation Fund and the grant component of the NRRP. Investments supported by European funds recorded a significant increase. Payments for projects financed under the 2021–2027 financial framework and through the NRRP, both from grants and loans, increased by RON 27 billion (+67.3%) compared with the same period of the previous year. This development offset the decrease in investments financed from national funds, which was influenced by the exceptionally high level of payments made at the beginning of 2025 to settle outstanding obligations, the capitalisation of Carpatica Feroviar România, and defence-related expenditure. Investment expenditure , which includes capital expenditure as well as expenditure related to development programmes financed from domestic and external sources, increased by RON 25.1 billion compared with the same period of the previous year, from RON 71.95 billion to RON 97.05 billion , of which 69.2% represents payments for projects financed from non-reimbursable external funds under the 2021–2027 framework. The eight-month budget execution data therefore indicate the continuation of the adjustment of the budget deficit, alongside a significant increase in revenues and the continued financing of projects through European funds and the NRRP. The reduction of the deficit by nearly RON 27 billion compared with the same period in 2025, and its decrease from 4.51% to 2.89% of GDP , are the main indicators of the fiscal and budgetary consolidation process during the first eight months of the year.
